sections.title: A Three-Phase Meeting
sections.content:
The memo proposes organizing the May Network Working Group meeting around advertised topics, status reports, and position papers. Its goal is to use the meeting time more effectively.

The planned phases cover updates from sites, discussion of current network-wide work, and consideration of new subjects for the group.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting is organized into three kinds of work: status updates, current issues, and new topics. This structure is meant to help participants use their time well.

sections.title: Reports and Discussion Topics
sections.content:
In the first phase, existing sites report on software, hardware, and network use, while new sites describe their plans. The memo estimates five to ten minutes for each site unless told otherwise and expects a short written report.

The second phase covers current topics such as the Network Information Center, Form Machine Telnet, and Logger Protocol. Committees should prepare reports, and people with other views should present position papers.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites and committees are asked to prepare short written and spoken updates. Participants can also submit position papers to make sure different views are heard.

sections.title: Preparing the Agenda
sections.content:
The third phase is for new topics, including long-term goals, near-term operational goals, and how much structure the group should have. Suggestions are especially welcome when introduced with a short position paper.

The memo asks for reports and position papers to be published as RFCs by May 1, 1971, where possible. The agenda and meeting schedule are to be published around that date.
sections.plainLanguage: Participants can propose new questions for the group to discuss. Written material is requested before the meeting so the agenda can be prepared.
